heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF SEMARANG CITY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Semarang City.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Semarang.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of Almighty God and are His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
6. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.
7. Protection of Women is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the private or public sphere.
9. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society.
10. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development.

CHAPTER VI

STRATEGIES FOR THE EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 23

1. The Empowerment and Protection of Women shall be implemented by integrating gender mainstreaming and gender-disaggregated data based on laws and regulations.
2. The Empowerment and Protection of Women shall be implemented with working groups and/or integrated services established by Mayor's Decree.
3. The Empowerment and Protection of Women shall be coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Empowerment and Protection of Women.

heading: Article 25

Article 25

1. The formulation of policy planning for programs and activities as referred to in Article 24 letter a, shall be implemented through:
a. mapping, collecting, processing and presenting data;
b. coordination and synchronization of the preparation of planning for programs and activities with related Regional Apparatus; and
c. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
2. The formulation of policy planning for programs and activities shall be implemented based on minimum service standards and standard operating procedures.
3. The formulation of policy planning for programs and activities for the implementation of the Empowerment and Protection of Women shall be coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of planning.

heading: Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

The implementation of programs and activities as referred to in Article 24 letter c, shall be implemented through:
a. implementation of programs and activities set forth in the budget documents of Regional Apparatus; and
b. coordination and synchronization of the implementation of programs and activities with related Regional Apparatus.

heading: Part Five
translated_text:
Part Five

Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting

heading: Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

The implementation of monitoring, evaluation and reporting as referred to in Article 24 letter d, shall be implemented through:
a. conducting monitoring and evaluation periodically on the implementation of programs and activities that have been carried out;
b. Reports shall be submitted at least 1 (one) time in 1 (one) year or at any time if necessary; and
c. evaluation results as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the following year.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 29

1. The Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Empowerment and Protection of Women functions as the leading sector in the implementation of the Empowerment and Protection of Women.
2. Further provisions regarding the implementation of the Empowerment and Protection of Women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

PARTICIPATION

Article 30

1. The community, community groups/community organizations, business sector, academics, and/or other professional groups may participate in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection.
2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. cooperation;
b. synergy;
c. provision of communication, information and education media regarding Women's Empowerment and Protection; and
d. active role in the fulfillment of women's rights through social responsibility.
3. Further provisions regarding participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated in a Mayor Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER X

translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

FUNDING

Article 32

Funding for the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other lawful and non-binding sources, in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF DRAFT REGIONAL REGULATION OF SEMARANG CITY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improved services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare while always taking into account the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, a governmental affair related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens have equal status in law and government and are obliged to uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equal status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation and decision-making process, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.
17- Based on this, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

heading: Article 2
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF DRAFT REGIONAL REGULATION OF SEMARANG CITY
translated_text:
Article 2

Point a
What is meant by "Principle of respect for human rights" contains the understanding that the Republic of Indonesia recognizes and upholds human rights and fundamental human freedoms as rights that are inherently attached to and inseparable from human beings, which must be protected, respected, and upheld for the enhancement of human dignity, welfare, happiness, and intelligence as well as justice.

Point b
What is meant by "Principle of non-discrimination" is that in providing protection to women and children victims of violence, there shall be no differentiation based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

Point c
What is meant by "Principle of gender equality and justice" is that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Point d
What is meant by "Principle of justice and legal certainty" contains the understanding that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, protection and fair legal treatment as well as obtaining legal certainty and equal treatment before the law.

Point e
What is meant by "Principle of benefit" contains the understanding that the regulation of women's empowerment policies must provide the greatest benefit for the welfare of society.

Point f
What is meant by "Principle of participation" contains the understanding that the entire process of policy formation and implementation must take into account the active participation of all components of society so as to obtain equal benefits in all fields of development and life.

Point g
What is meant by "Principle of accountability" concerns that the implementation of women's empowerment must be accountable and constitutes part of the accountability for the implementation of government.

Point h
What is meant by "Principle of inclusion" is that the implementation of women's empowerment and protection is carried out by inviting and involving all people with various diversities of abilities, backgrounds, characteristics, status, conditions, ethnicity, culture and others as well as facilitating special needs based on such diversity and eliminating barriers that may hinder the equality of every woman in obtaining their rights.

Article 14

Point a

Point b
What is meant by the basic rights of workers includes:
a. the basic right to obtain decent wages.
b. the right to obtain equal opportunities and treatment from the company without discrimination.
c. the right to obtain work training to improve and develop work competence.
d. the right to perform work according to the determined time.
e. the right to placement of workers.
f. the right to obtain protection for occupational health and safety.
g. the right to obtain welfare through workers' social security.
h. the right to participate in trade unions or labor unions.
i. the right to obtain leave: at least 12 working days after the employee has worked for one year continuously.
j. the right to rest: workers after working four hours continuously, get the opportunity to rest for a minimum of half an hour.
k. the right to maternity leave, miscarriage leave and menstrual leave specifically for female workers/laborers: Female workers/laborers have the right to obtain rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months before the time of childbirth and 1.5 (one and a half) months after giving birth according to the calculation of an obstetrician or midwife.

Female workers/laborers who experience a miscarriage have the right to obtain rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months or in accordance with a certificate from an obstetrician or midwife.

Female workers/laborers who experience pain during menstruation and notify the employer, are not obliged to work on the first and second days during menstruation.

l. the right to perform worship.  m. the right to conduct strikes.  n. the right to obtain severance pay in the event of termination of employment or layoffs.  o. the right to a proper opportunity to provide breast milk to their child if this must be done during working hours.
